faqs.q: What's the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?

Understanding these codes is essential for API development, debugging network issues, and building robust web applications. This reference tool lets you quickly look up any status code, understand its meaning, and learn when to use it in your own APIs. faqs.q: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
faqs.a: 401 Unauthorized means the client has not provided valid authentication credentials. 403 Forbidden means the client is authenticated but does not have permission to access the resource.

faqs.q: When should I use 200 vs 201 vs 204?

faqs.q: What does a 502 Bad Gateway error mean?

This calculator takes an IP address with a CIDR prefix (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) and instantly computes the subnet mask, network address, broadcast address, first and last usable host, and total number of hosts. faqs.q: How do I calculate the number of hosts in a subnet?
faqs.a: The formula is 2^(32-prefix) - 2 for IPv4. The subtraction accounts for the network address and broadcast address. A /24 subnet has 2^8 - 2 = 254 usable hosts.

faqs.q: What is the difference between network and broadcast address?
faqs.a: The network address is the first address in a subnet (all host bits 0) and identifies the subnet. The broadcast address is the last (all host bits 1) and sends packets to all hosts in the subnet.

faqs.q: Which HMAC algorithm should I use?

Converting CSS to JS objects requires changing property names from kebab-case to camelCase (font-size becomes fontSize), wrapping string values in quotes, and converting pixel values to numbers where appropriate. This tool automates the conversion process, handling selectors, property names, and values. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How are CSS property names converted?

faqs.q: Are pixel values converted to numbers?

Converting XML to JSON is useful when migrating legacy systems, consuming SOAP APIs, or processing XML feeds in modern JavaScript applications. This tool parses XML and converts it to a structured JSON representation where elements become objects, attributes are prefixed with @, text content is stored as #text, and repeated elements automatically become arrays.
